title: Opinion on the re-evaluation of sodium carboxy methyl cellulose (E 466) as a food additive in foods for infants below 16 weeks of age and follow-up of its re-evaluation as food additive for uses in foods for all population groups
authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Flavourings (FAF), Younes M, Aquilina G, Castle L, Degen G, Engel KH, et al.
funder: European Food Safety Authority; requestor: European Commission.
result: The mouse studies of carboxymethylcellulose gave inconsistent results on fasting glucose, spleen weight, colon length and fat-pad weight, with small effects, and were obtained under non-blinded conditions with a high risk of bias. In the 11-day human study, glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, six cytokines, anti-lipopolysaccharide and anti-flagellin IgG and body weight were unchanged. The Panel considered that the preliminary results do not allow identifying specific health concerns and that the field needs investigation on a large scale.
